chat.answer:
**Amount in the document (Indian grouping):** 4,18,25,000 rupees — page 6

**Restated in the crore system:** ₹4,18,25,000 = **4.1825 crore rupees** (₹4.1825 cr, i.e. 4 crore 18 lakh 25 thousand)

**Restated with international grouping:** **INR 41,825,000** (forty-one million eight hundred twenty-five thousand rupees)

Both spellings are the identical figure: 4 × 10⁷ + 1 × 10⁶ + 8 × 10⁵ + 2 × 10³ + 5 × 10² = 41,825,000. The other numbers on the earlier pages (1.4 million m³, 3.1 ppt, 62%, 18.4/44.0/12.6 m³/s, 12.7/3.9/51.2 NTU, 740 mm, 12.5 km², 25 °C, pH 7.4, 0.84 dS/m) are volumes, concentrations and physical parameters, not monetary amounts, so page 6 is the only place a rupee figure appears.

Caveat worth flagging: this is OCR output from a scan (the appendix note on page 5 says the borehole log came from a hand-written field notebook), so if the grouping digits matter legally, verify against the original scan — the crore/lakh comma pattern is one of the things OCR can misread.
